neighbours.label: Wildlife management that moves wild animals into or between wild habitats: releasing, relocating, tagging-and-release, stocking waters and hatchery rearing for the wild (firing on 'release(d)', 'into', the moved animals); pets, zoo and farm animals handled in the same way stay quiet.
fire: Biologists relocated the wolves to a remote valley in the north.
The trust breeds otters in pens and then frees them along the river.
Each autumn the agency stocks the mountain lakes with young trout.
Volunteers carried the rescued hedgehogs back to the woods.
The hatchery rears sturgeon to restore the river's wild population.
Rangers darted the rhinos and flew them to a new reserve.
Rehabilitated seals were set free on the beach at dawn.
Conservationists reintroduced lynx into the forest last year.
quiet: The family moved their dog to a new house in the north.
The zoo breeds otters in pens and shows them to visitors.
Each autumn the farm fills its ponds with ducks for the market.
Volunteers carried the kittens back to the shelter.
The pet shop rears goldfish for home aquariums.
Vets sedated the zoo's rhino and moved it to a new pen.
The ponies were led into the stable at dusk.
The breeder introduced a new rooster into the henhouse last year.

short: moving animals into the wild (release, relocate, stock)
notes: Round 2 for this pole (round 1, sweep 1: 'releasing animals into the wild' failed on near misses: tagging sea turtles 0.41, a hatchery counting fry 0.33, while all 8 releases fired, median 0.75). Refinement probe: tagging and moving bears 0.50, hatchery salmon for the river 0.26, stocking a reservoir 0.23; pet cat 0.000, zoo enclosure 0.04, farmer moving cows 0.09. New label: the wider wildlife-release setting; near misses keep the handling of animals but make them pets, zoo or farm animals.
